title: Automation
goal: Automation lanes with Write, Touch, Latch and Trim passes recorded as single revisions, with the documented precision per target. It also completes the toolbox of the UI mockup: the Draw tool with the lanes, and the Range Selection, Zoom, Mute and Play tools, which M5b's usable release leaves out (decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-18; UI redesign 10.11).
specSections: Two channels into the audio thread
prerequisites: M2; M4 for plugin parameter automation.
M5b for the UI features: the toolbar, the Glue and Erase tools and the editing commands of m5b-ui-edit-more.

features.title: Automation lanes in the document and segments in the graph
acceptance: Breakpoint lanes compile to preevaluated segments; built-in targets are sample-accurate; interpolation domains as specified; offline and realtime renders agree.

features.title: Write, Touch, Latch and Trim passes
acceptance: Captured values go through automationOutbox with an end marker; one automation.write_pass revision per pass after thinning; no tail values lost.

features.title: Precision contract per format
acceptance: CLAP sample-accurate, VST3 and AU block-accurate through JUCE, documented and exposed to users and agents; tests measure the actual precision.

features.title: Clip mute in the document: clip.set_mute (the mute half of E-9)
acceptance: Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-18 (UI redesign 10.11): the mute half of E-9, which no milestone owned, is this feature. A clip has a muted flag in the document, omitted while false so earlier documents and their hashes are unchanged; the document version rule of the architecture spec decides whether the schema version moves.

clip.set_mute {clipId, muted} is one revision declaring exactly that clip, undoable, usable as a plan step with a preview, and listed by command.list; engine.capabilities lists features.clipMute. An unknown clip is not_found and a non-boolean muted is invalid_params.

A muted clip is silent in realtime playback and in an offline render, and the two renders are equal (null test); unmuting restores it sample for sample; the graph change needs no stop of the transport.

The muted flag survives save and reopen, replay gives the same document hash, and rollback and undo restore it. docs/schemas and the architecture spec's siann-model and Commands text carry the field, the command and the feature flag, and the MCP adapter reaches the command through execute.

features.title: The rest of the toolbox: the Range Selection, Zoom, Mute and Play tools
acceptance: Key 2 chooses the Range Selection tool: a drag selects a range of time over one or several tracks, snapped as an edit is, and Delete Time, Cut Time, Insert Silence, Crop and Split Range act on it, each a composition of the existing clip commands in one command.execute and one revision, restored by one undo (a unit test per command builder, an e2e per operation).
Key 6 chooses the Zoom tool: a click zooms in around the pointer, Alt-click zooms out, a drag zooms to the dragged range; it changes the view only and sends no request.

Key 7 chooses the Mute tool: a click toggles the clicked clip's mute and a drag over several clips sets them to the state the first one took, as one command.execute of clip.set_mute and one revision; Shift+M, Shift+U and Alt+M mute, unmute and toggle the selection. A muted clip is drawn dimmed, as the mockup's draw() draws a clip of a muted track. Against capabilities without features.clipMute or the command clip.set_mute the tool is not in the DOM and its box stays empty (UI redesign 3.0), while the other three tools, which need no engine method, are rendered.

Key 9 chooses the Play tool: holding the pointer on a clip plays from that position until release, then playback stops and the cursor returns to where it was; with no audio device the tool is disabled with a tooltip naming the reason.
F9 and F10 choose the previous and the next tool. 1 still returns to Object Selection, and no tool key fires from a text field.
Every new string is in the three catalogs, and the tour appends its states after the last M5b state. Tour states changed: the toolbar in every state.

Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-18 (UI redesign 10.11): tools 2, 6, 7 and 9 of the mockup belong to this feature; until it lands they are absent and their boxes stay empty under their hold tokens. Ported from the mockup's markup (decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-17; UI redesign 10.9; docs/harness/agent-rules.md, "UI fidelity"): this feature's parts, tool-2, tool-6, tool-7, tool-9, take the DOM structure, class names and data-part ids mockup.html gives them, are styled by the shared rules of app/renderer/ui and are wired to real data; a unit test holds the rendered structure to the mockup's markup and an e2e assertion finds each id in the window. Their gate in app/test/fidelity/manifest.json (m6a-ui-tools) goes from pending to report in this pull request and the --hold-* tokens of these parts are deleted; nothing sets a gate to enforce. A side-by-side screenshot of the app and the mockup is attached for each state this feature changes, in en and zh-TW, with the fidelity report; the maintainer reviews it by eye, and no geometry or pixel result blocks.

features.title: Automation in the UI: R and W on headers, strips and the Inspector, and lanes in the event display
acceptance: R and W on each track header, on each MixConsole strip (the master included) and in the Inspector, with the Inspector's Automation section, show and set the track's automation read and write state from the engine (W red when armed), following other connections, undo and applied plans.

A lane opens from the arrow at the header's lower-left corner; its points and segments are edited with the Object Selection and Draw tools (key 8 chooses the Draw tool, which this feature lands: it adds and drags automation points), each edit one revision restored by one undo, and a write pass appears as one revision when it ends.

Against capabilities without the automation methods none of these controls is in the DOM and their space stays empty (UI redesign 3.0, decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-15), as it has been since M5 (e2e with a reduced capabilities fixture).
Every new string is in the three catalogs, and the tour appends its states after the last M5b state.

Decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-15: the automation parts of the mockup belong to this feature. Ported from the mockup's markup (decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-17; UI redesign 10.9; docs/harness/agent-rules.md, "UI fidelity"): this feature's parts, *-read, *-write, strip-*-automation, inspector-automation, and tool-8, the Draw tool (decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-18; UI redesign 10.11), take the DOM structure, class names and data-part ids mockup.html gives them, are styled by the shared rules of app/renderer/ui and are wired to real data; a unit test holds the rendered structure to the mockup's markup and an e2e assertion finds each id in the window. Their gate in app/test/fidelity/manifest.json (m6a-ui-automation) goes from pending to report in this pull request and the --hold-* tokens of these parts are deleted; nothing sets a gate to enforce. A side-by-side screenshot of the app and the mockup is attached for each state this feature changes, in en and zh-TW, with the fidelity report; the maintainer reviews it by eye, and no geometry or pixel result blocks.

exit.text: Automation passes are recorded as single revisions; precision is documented per format.
